items.title: Integrating QPUs into Supercomputing Centers Using Slurm HRES Plugins
items.summary: Slurm 26.11 introduces Hierarchical Resources (HRES) plugins to model quantum processing units (QPUs) as native, cluster-level schedulable resources. HRES associates a QPU with specific nodes, resolving limitations of generic resources and license-based approaches. A short Lua plugin handles device health checks and job admission, keeping site-specific policies separate in `resources.yaml`. Community projects like QRMI and QDMI have created open-source plugins to connect Slurm clusters to various quantum providers. This framework allows HPC systems to schedule QPUs seamlessly by treating them as a single schedulable unit.

items.title: Co-Designing Sparse Attention for Efficient Long-Context Inference
items.summary: Sparse attention moves the cost of attention to an indexer, which requires optimizing the indexer and Top-k selection for efficient GPU inference. Key design choices involve balancing compute and memory by controlling parameters like group size ($G$), head dimension ($H_{sz}$), and compression ratio ($CR$). Guidelines suggest using $KH=1$, $H_{sz}=128$ or $256$, and employing block-level selection for better key fetching. Fusing Top-k into the indexer and using speculative decoding further accelerate inference. Overall efficiency is achieved by reducing the number of keys scored through compression and sharing.

The design centers on moving the attention cost to an indexer, requiring optimization of the indexer and Top-k selection for efficient GPU inference. Key design choices involve balancing compute and memory by controlling parameters such as group size, head dimension, and compression ratio. Guidelines suggest utilizing settings like $KH=1$ and head dimensions of one hundred twenty-eight or two hundred fifty-six, alongside employing block-level selection for improved key fetching. items.title: Helping AI text detectors keep up with changing conditions
items.summary: Researchers demonstrated that test-time adaptation allows AI text detectors to become more robust against changing writing styles and adversarial attempts by AI users. This method enables a detection model to learn from new, unlabeled data on the fly without needing a full retraining from scratch. Experiments showed that TTA increased accuracy significantly, achieving 93% accuracy in detecting disguised text versus only 27% with traditional methods. This adaptation helps detectors cope with distribution shifts caused by evolving human and AI writing habits. While promising, researchers caution that future challenges remain regarding the difficulty of tracking subtle linguistic shifts.

items.title: From tasks to goals
items.summary: Moving from tasks to goals involves shifting from specifying actions to outcomes and from bounded assignments to ongoing responsibilities for agents. Agents pursuing goals need mechanisms to interact with humans for clarification, receive feedback, and be triggered by events or time, necessitating robust scheduling. Furthermore, agents managing ongoing responsibilities require memory to compound past decisions and feedback effectively. Ultimately, delegating goals requires a shift in the user's role to setting direction and reviewing progress rather than specifying individual steps.

items.title: What should AI be to us?
items.summary: Discussions surrounding AI consciousness explore how humans relate to artificial intelligence, with general consensus from institutions suggesting current AI systems do not possess human-like thought or feeling. Researchers suggest models may have separate conscious and unconscious processes, and some evidence points to their capacity to process concepts like pain. The central debate shifts to what AI should be to humanity, ranging from tools to potential successors or companions. This uncertainty drives calls for empirical research and policies regarding AI welfare and rights. Ultimately, the field is grappling with defining "flourishing" and the implications of creating potentially sentient digital entities.
